item.title: Is a Two-Sample t-Test Appropriate? Quiz Scores for Two Study Formats
item.stimulus: An instructor believes that students who study with practice tests earn a greater mean quiz score than students who study by rereading. Thousands of students at the university use each format. The instructor independently and randomly selected 32 students who use practice tests (sample mean 78.5 points) and 15 students who reread (sample mean 74.1 points). A dotplot of the 32 practice-test scores shows no strong skewness and no outliers. A dotplot of the 15 rereading scores is skewed right with one outlier.

parts.prompt: Let μ₁ be the mean for the practice-test format and μ₂ the mean for the rereading format. Define the parameters of interest and state the null and alternative hypotheses for the test.

criteria.text: Defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean quiz score, in points, of all students at the university who study with practice tests, and μ₂ is the true mean quiz score of all students at the university who study by rereading.
criteria.evidence: Response defines μ₁ and μ₂ as the μ₁ is the true mean quiz score, in points, of all students at the university who study with practice tests, and μ₂ is the true mean quiz score of all students at the university who study by rereading, naming the response variable and the population in context.
criteria.fix: Name the parameter with its symbol and say which population mean (or mean difference) it is, in context.

criteria.text: States H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 and Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ > 0.
criteria.evidence: Response writes H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 and Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ > 0, with the alternative in the correct direction.
criteria.fix: Write the null with an equals sign and take the direction of the alternative from the question being investigated.

parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate procedure, and decide whether its conditions are met. Justify each decision.

criteria.text: Identifies the appropriate procedure as a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means.
criteria.evidence: Response names a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means.
criteria.fix: Name the procedure from the data design: one sample, matched pairs (analyze the differences), or two independent samples.

criteria.text: Checks the randomization condition: the students were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of students.
criteria.evidence: Response states the randomization condition in context: the students were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of students.
criteria.fix: Check that the data came from random selection or random assignment, and say how, in context.

criteria.text: Checks the 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of students in its group.
criteria.evidence: Response checks that the sample size is less than 10% of the population: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of students in its group.
criteria.fix: When sampling without replacement, compare each sample size with 10% of its population to confirm independence.

criteria.text: Checks the sample-data condition: one sample (n = 15) is less than 30, so both samples must show no strong skewness or outliers, but the rereading sample has an outlier, so the sample-data condition is not met and the two-sample t-test is not appropriate.
criteria.evidence: Response states the sample-data condition, says whether it is met, and gives the reason: one sample (n = 15) is less than 30, so both samples must show no strong skewness or outliers, but the rereading sample has an outlier, so the sample-data condition is not met and the two-sample t-test is not appropriate.
criteria.fix: State the condition that applies: sample sizes of at least 30, or samples with no strong skewness or outliers.

item.model_answer:
(a) Μ₁ is the true mean quiz score, in points, of all students at the university who study with practice tests, and μ₂ is the true mean quiz score of all students at the university who study by rereading. H₀: μ₁ − μ₂ = 0 versus Hₐ: μ₁ − μ₂ > 0.

(b) The procedure is a two-sample t-test for a difference in population means. Randomization: the students were selected by independent random samples from the two groups of students. 10% condition: each sample is less than 10% of the thousands of students in its group. Sample-data condition: one sample (n = 15) is less than 30, so both samples must show no strong skewness or outliers, but the rereading sample has an outlier, so the sample-data condition is not met and the two-sample t-test is not appropriate.
item.verification_python:
n1, n2 = 32, 15
both_big = min(n1, n2) >= 30
assert both_big == False
assert 78.5 > 74.1
print("ALL_CHECKS_PASSED")
